request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 37.6% (95% band 30.1% to 41.7%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.302: -0.6; 0.302 <= x < 0.569: -0.13; 0.569 <= x < 0.676: +0.613; 0.676 <= x < 0.735: +1.5; x >= 0.735: +3.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.93, 95% band [+3.23, +4.39]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 23.1% (95% band 14.5% to 28.0%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; >= 1: +0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.81, 95% band [+0.54, +1.07]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 16.3% (95% band 10.9% to 18.8%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 41,400: +0.26; 41,400 <= x < 83,900: -0.11; x >= 83,900: -0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.92, 95% band [-1.23, -0.53]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 7.5% (95% band 3.8% to 10.6%); rank 4 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 240: +0.012; x >= 240: 0 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.49, 95% band [-0.74, -0.19]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 4.2% (95% band 1.0% to 7.4%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.18, 95% band [-0.01, +0.43]).
- `num_dependents`: number of dependents (standardised).
  Share of importance 3.9% (95% band 1.6% to 6.9%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.03, 95% band [-0.38, +0.21]).
- `months_at_address`: months at the current address (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.3% to 5.2%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.07, 95% band [-0.15, +0.25]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.4% to 4.2%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.08, 95% band [-0.39, +0.11]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 0.1% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.00, 95% band [-0.05, +0.11]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 3.9%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0986 to 0.751: +3.81 (95% band +3.13 to +4.33) when `history_months` = 23.5, +4.16 (95% band +3.23 to +4.94) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 343: -0.73 (95% band -1.30 to -0.22) when `utilization` = 0.0986, -0.38 (95% band -0.63 to -0.01) when `utilization` = 0.751.
- `months_at_address & num_dependents`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `months_at_address` from -1.64 to 1.67: -0.09 (95% band -0.51 to +0.23) when `num_dependents` = -1.63, +0.13 (95% band -0.20 to +0.49) when `num_dependents` = 1.62.
  Effect of `num_dependents` from -1.63 to 1.62: -0.19 (95% band -0.63 to +0.15) when `months_at_address` = -1.64, +0.02 (95% band -0.41 to +0.27) when `months_at_address` = 1.67.
- `utilization & dti`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0986 to 0.751: +3.84 (95% band +3.18 to +4.39) when `dti` = 0.0282, +3.85 (95% band +3.21 to +4.41) when `dti` = 0.572.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0282 to 0.572: +0.17 (95% band -0.18 to +0.42) when `utilization` = 0.0986, +0.18 (95% band -0.09 to +0.44) when `utilization` = 0.751.
- `income & num_dependents`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.0%).
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 112,000: -0.86 (95% band -1.19 to -0.48) when `num_dependents` = -1.63, -0.93 (95% band -1.27 to -0.53) when `num_dependents` = 1.62.
  Effect of `num_dependents` from -1.63 to 1.62: -0.04 (95% band -0.53 to +0.22) when `income` = 22,000, -0.11 (95% band -0.60 to +0.24) when `income` = 112,000.
- `income & age`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 1.9%).
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 112,000: -0.88 (95% band -1.25 to -0.52) when `age` = 23.7, -0.88 (95% band -1.21 to -0.51) when `age` = 72.2.
  Effect of `age` from 23.7 to 72.2: -0.10 (95% band -0.41 to +0.15) when `income` = 22,000, -0.10 (95% band -0.41 to +0.13) when `income` = 112,000.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by revolving credit utilization, the share of the credit limit an applicant is using, which accounts for about 38% of the model's importance; the risk rises sharply once utilization passes roughly 0.68, and above 0.735 it adds the largest push toward default of any feature."},{"id":2,"text":"Past delinquencies are the second strongest driver (about 23% of importance): having any delinquency on the credit file raises predicted risk noticeably compared with none."},{"id":3,"text":"Annual income is the third driver (about 16% of importance): incomes below roughly $41,400 push risk up, while incomes above roughly $83,900 pull it down, with the effect fairly consistent across the range of other features."},{"id":4,"text":"Length of credit history matters less (about 7.5% of importance, with a wide uncertainty band), and its effect is modest: shorter histories below 240 months add a small amount of risk."},{"id":5,"text":"Debt-to-income ratio, number of dependents, months at address, age, and recent credit inquiries have effects the data do not resolve from zero at this sample size, so they should not be treated as reliable drivers of these predictions."},{"id":6,"text":"The model contains a few interactions, but they are small: the effect of utilization is somewhat stronger for applicants with longer credit histories, and the effect of income is similar across ages and family sizes, so the main story is additive."},{"id":7,"text":"The uncertainty bands on the ranking are wide for some features, so the exact order of the lower-ranked drivers, and whether history length matters at all, is not firmly settled by the data."}]}
